questions.question: In a young adult with hyperglycaemia, glycosuria, BMI 24.6 kg/m2, negative GAD and IA-2 antibodies, preserved stimulated C-peptide, and diabetes affecting multiple successive relatives diagnosed before age 30, what specific form of diabetes should be suspected, and what inheritance pattern is typical?
Which clinical and laboratory features in this case make HNF1A-MODY more likely than classic type 1 diabetes and more likely than typical type 2 diabetes?

When MODY is suspected in a patient with early-onset diabetes, what initial workup should be obtained before genetic testing, and how do autoantibody testing and C-peptide measurement help determine whether sequencing is warranted?
How do HNF1A mutations lead to both progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction and glycosuria, and why is postprandial hyperglycaemia often prominent early in the disease?

How should a glucagon-stimulated C-peptide increase from 0.39 to 0.83 nmol/L be interpreted in this patient, and why is this test supportive rather than definitive for distinguishing MODY from early type 1 diabetes?

A previously unreported HNF1A missense variant was identified in this patient. What types of evidence can support classifying a novel variant as pathogenic or likely pathogenic under ACMG principles, even if it is absent from ClinVar?

After genetic confirmation of HNF1A-MODY in a patient initially treated with basal insulin, metformin, and a DPP-4 inhibitor, how should therapy be reconsidered, and why can insulin often be discontinued once glycaemic control is achieved?
Why are low-dose sulfonylureas traditionally considered first-line therapy in HNF1A-MODY, and in what clinical circumstances might a GLP-1 receptor agonist be a preferable alternative?
Why should SGLT2 inhibitors be used cautiously or avoided in patients with HNF1A-MODY?
Once HNF1A-MODY is diagnosed in one patient, what is the rationale for cascade testing and counselling of family members, and which relatives should be prioritised?
